tiering.note: Within a position, a new tier starts wherever the point drop-off to the next-best player exceeds (average drop-off + this many standard deviations of drop-off). Raise this to get fewer/bigger tiers, lower it for more/smaller tiers.

season.note: Used to convert a defense's season-total points allowed into a per-game average for the points_allowed_buckets lookup, then scale the bucket result back up across the season. start_date (approximate NFL Week 1 kickoff) seeds the site's default 'current week' for This Week / Rest of Season views -- users can override it directly in League Details, this is just a starting guess.

roster.note: Starter counts per position (BN excluded from replacement-level math since it can hold any position).

notes: CONFIRMED as of 2026-07-26 against the league's real rules document (FOOTBALL_RULES_2023-2024.docx), with a direct user correction on the 60+ FG value. Passing/rushing/receiving/roster/D-ST points-allowed all matched the prior placeholder values exactly. FG buckets were corrected to add the 60+ yard tier -- worth 15pts (not the doc's written 9), a huge premium over 5pts for 50-59 -- that the placeholder didn't have. extra_point_returned corrected from a guessed 2 down to 0 -- not a scored category in the real rules.

Re-confirmed 2026-07-27 (session 6): user explicitly re-verified the 60+ yard / 15pt tier stays -- it's a real differentiator that mattered to their actual payout in a real week last season, not a rounding-error edge case. Do not simplify/merge it away again without asking.

The real rules also specify a 2-point-conversion rule where EVERY player involved gets 2 points (e.g. both the QB who threw it and the receiver who caught it) -- this already matches how two_point_conversion is applied per-player in the scoring engine, no change needed there.

IMPORTANT data-source caveat given the 60+ tier is now worth 3x the 50-59 tier: our stats source only reports one aggregate '50+ yard' field goal make count, with no way to split out true 60+ yard makes. See optimizer/schema.py's FG_INPUT_BANDS comment -- the aggregate is conservatively treated as 50-59 yard makes (5pts) rather than 60+ (15pts) to avoid overvaluing kickers, but this means genuine 60+ specialists are currently UNDERVALUED since their bonus isn't captured at all. Worth sourcing real distance-level kicker data (e.g. per-game logs) if accuracy here matters enough -- flagged again session 6 since the user says this real gap has cost real money, so it's worth prioritizing over other polish.
The rules doc is titled '2023-2024' -- worth double-checking with the user whether anything changed for the current season.
Edit the bucket lists freely -- add/remove/adjust rows, the scoring engine reads them at runtime and does not assume a fixed number of buckets.
Passing interceptions are not scored here because the league's INT penalty (if any) was not provided -- add a 'interception' key under scoring.passing if the real league docks points for it.

Rookie projections (2026-07-26): players with zero real NFL stats (this year's incoming draft class) are projected from NFL draft capital alone -- averaged rookie-year stats of past draftees in the same round-group + position, from optimizer/rookie_projections.py. Tagged 'R' in Rankings/Mock Draft/Team Rosters. Two known limitations: (1) it's round+position only, no college production or combine data, so e.g. two round-1 WRs in the same draft class get an identical projection; (2) the training data (fetch_actuals.py) only captures rookies who ranked highly enough to appear on a stats leaderboard, so late-round baselines skew optimistic (rookies who got zero playing time are simply absent, not a real zero, so they don't drag the average down).

ADP + Value vs ADP (updated 2026-07-27): 'ADP' is consensus Average Draft Position from Fantasy Football Calculator's free API (scripts/fetch_adp.py, data/historical/adp.csv), attribution: fantasyfootballcalculator.com -- specifically their '2qb' format, real empirical ADP from actual 2-QB-format drafts, since this league starts 2 QBs and a generic 1-QB PPR list would misvalue QBs badly. Their non-PPR-leaning default also better matches this league's 0-points-per-reception scoring than a PPR list would. Unlike the original ESPN-based source, FFC genuinely has historical year-specific data (2020-2024, data/historical/{year}_adp.csv) -- 2025 has no 2QB data at FFC and is skipped, and historical years default to a 12-team pool (FFC doesn't archive 10-team-specific historical drafts) rather than erroring, so treat historical ADP as directionally useful, not exact. Coverage is real-draft-sample-limited (~200 players currently have enough 2QB-format drafts at FFC to report ADP, well short of our full ~550-player pool) -- deep-bench/rookie-model players without a real ADP show as unranked rather than a fabricated number. 'Value vs ADP' compares a player's VOR to the VOR our own model has at whoever it ranks at that same ADP slot -- positive means our model likes this player more than the market does (a potential value/sleeper at their current ADP), negative means the market is drafting them ahead of where our own model would. It is NOT blended into VOR/rankings itself -- it's a separate comparison signal, so the market's opinion never silently overrides our own real-stats-driven model.
